dedupe_keys.name: acclimate global supply chain loss propagation model

description: Acclimate is a numerical, dynamic agent-based model of how economic losses cascade through the global supply network, developed at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research. National or regional sectors act as firms and consumers as agents, and the network of trade and supply relations is built from empirical input-output data that give the unperturbed baseline. The model simulates the spread of production losses caused by local demand, supply or price shocks such as floods, heatwaves and tropical cyclones; its reference paper (Otto, Willner, Wenz, Frieler and Levermann, Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control, 2017) found that indirect losses can match direct ones but can be mitigated by warehousing and idle capacities. The code is archived on Zenodo (version 3.4.0, 16 July 2024, AGPL-3.0), with a geographic transportation module and maritime network data as separate records under CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: running it needs input-output data, shock scenarios and compilation of the code, and results depend on behavioural parameters. For simulation it models dynamic, global cascading economic losses from climate extremes and supply disruptions. Related catalogue records include BoARIO, EXIOBASE and Eora2.
